title: How to use Gopher when a manual is the authority
summary: Do not guess a chapter/page workflow. Use find/locate to resolve a bounded location, read it, move around it for context, then return to the original task.
procedure: If you know a phrase or command name, run `gopher reference find <file-or-url> <string>`.
If you know a printed/manual page but PDF front matter shifts physical pages, run `reference locate --reference-page N --approx-page M --window K`.
Run `reference read` on the returned physical_page or HTML section.
Use `reference move` with -1, +1, -5, +5 (or another bounded delta) to inspect continuation/context.
Return to the originating sphere/article and apply the evidence to the coding/reasoning task.
invariants: PDF navigation is by physical page. Printed/manual page is a separate approximate reference identity.
HTTP(S) and local files use the same operation shapes.
